sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Healthcare is emerging as the market's most resilient leader with sustained momentum and a +2 rank improvement, while top-ranked Energy shows signs of underlying instability.

Defensive and growth-oriented sectors are showing diverging trends. Healthcare and Energy are the only two "all-green" sectors out of 11, demonstrating positive performance across all timeframes. Healthcare is particularly dominant, recognized as the sole sustained strong sector across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons, climbing two spots to rank 5 with a leading momentum score of 0.83. 

Conversely, Financials and Communication Services are fading. Financials dropped two spots to rank 8, while Communication Services slid to the bottom of the board at rank 11 with a weak momentum score of 0.22. Meanwhile, Consumer Cyclical and Consumer Defensive saw minor rank improvements but remain firmly in laggard territory.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Only 2 of 11 groups—Healthcare (momentum 0.83) and Energy (momentum 0.82)—are positive across the week, month, quarter, half, and YTD.
* **Sustained Leadership:** Healthcare is the only sector categorized as sustained strong across 1-, 3-, and 6-month rankings.
* **Top Momentum:** Energy (0.82) and Basic Materials (0.75) join Healthcare as the top momentum leaders, holding the YTD rank 1 and rank 3 spots respectively.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Healthcare improved +2 spots to rank 5 (momentum 0.83). Consumer Cyclical (rank 10, momentum 0.35) and Consumer Defensive (rank 7, momentum 0.33) each gained +1 spot.
* **Top Losers:** Financials dropped -2 spots to rank 8 (momentum 0.48), while Real Estate (rank 6, momentum 0.50) and Communication Services (rank 11, momentum 0.22) both fell -1 spot.
* **Momentum Laggards:** Utilities remains the weakest sector with a momentum score of 0.13 (rank 9), followed closely by Communication Services at 0.22.

## Divergences
* **Energy Fragility:** Despite holding the rank 1 spot and being "all-green," Energy exhibits a low agreement score of 0.44, signaling a fragile and unstable trend.
* **Flat Leaders:** Technology (rank 2, momentum 0.65) and Basic Materials (rank 3, momentum 0.75) held their ranks flat over the last 5 sessions, pointing to a pause in their upward momentum.

rotation_phase.label: Late Cycle
rotation_phase.reasoning: Energy and Basic Materials are leading momentum alongside Healthcare, fitting a late-stage expansion where commodity-linked sectors outperform.

pulse.headline: Weak sector breadth and fragile energy leadership drag down conviction.

conviction.why: Conviction is pressured by a low 18% all-green breadth, a mean rank agreement of 0.59, and one fragile divergence.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive commodities and biotech are surging into leadership, while high-end consumer discretionary and travel sectors suffer severe weekly momentum breakdowns.

On August 19, 2026, US industry breadth remains highly concentrated, with only 17 of 143 groups maintaining all-green status across all timeframes. Energy and defensive sectors are driving the market's upper echelon, led by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.955) and Biotechnology (momentum 0.923). Rapid rotations are favoring resource-linked groups, highlighted by Coking Coal jumping 42 spots and Gold gaining 29 spots over the last five sessions.

Conversely, consumer-facing and cyclical groups are experiencing a sharp rotation out of favor. Luxury Goods fell a staggering 54 spots to rank 114, while Airlines plunged 30 spots to rank 113. This capital flight is accompanied by early-warning signs in industrial cyclicals like Metal Fabrication and Steel, which are slipping in rank despite holding relatively high momentum scores.

## Strength
* **All-Green Leadership:** Only 17 of 143 groups are green across all timeframes, led by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.96), Biotechnology (momentum 0.92), and Silver (momentum 0.90).
* **Sustained Performance:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing, Biotechnology, Staffing & Employment Services, and Coking Coal continue to demonstrate long-term regime strength, ranking in the top 35 across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
* **Defensive Health Dominance:** Drug Manufacturers - General (momentum 0.83) and Health Information Services (momentum 0.81) have solidified their all-green status alongside Biotechnology.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Resource Surge:** Coking Coal (+42 spots to rank 71, momentum 0.83) and Gold (+29 spots to rank 50, momentum 0.77) led the weekly gainers, alongside Biotechnology (+14 spots to rank 26).
* **Discretionary Capitulation:** Luxury Goods plummeted 54 spots to rank 114 (momentum 0.22), while Airlines dropped 30 spots to rank 113 (momentum 0.32) and Apparel Retail fell 21 spots to rank 109.
* **Entrenched Laggards:** Airports & Air Services (momentum 0.061, rank 139) and Advertising Agencies (momentum 0.127, rank 143) remain anchored at the bottom of the YTD rankings.

## Divergences
* **Fading Cyclicals:** Metal Fabrication (momentum 0.63, rank -8 in 5d) and Steel (momentum 0.71, rank -4 in 5d) are showing early fatigue, losing rank despite positive nominal momentum.
* **Emerging Value:** Specialty Business Services (+20 spots, momentum 0.46) and REIT - Residential (+12 spots, momentum 0.45) are climbing rapidly in rank from low momentum baselines.
* **Fragile All-Green:** Oil & Gas Integrated holds an all-green signal but exhibits weak underlying support, carrying a low agreement score of just 0.48.
